title: Customer status stepdown and clarity notes (post-incident) - 2026-04-01
body:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, customer-facing update + internal checklist to be used during stepdown from active incident to monitoring and then to closure. It is written to be repurposed into (a) status page update, (b) short email to affected customers, and (c) key-account outreach talking points.

TL;DR (customer-facing):
We experienced elevated API error rates and increased latencies affecting text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 between 2026-03-31 03:20 UTC and 2026-03-31 06:05 UTC. Normal service resumed at ~06:05 UTC. We have implemented mitigations and ongoing monitoring; no customer data loss has been identified.

Suggested status page update (short):
Title: Partial service disruption impacting inference in eu-west-1 – resolved
Status: Resolved
Details: Between 03:20 and 06:05 UTC on 2026-03-31 some requests to text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 returned errors or experienced higher than normal latency. Our automatic routing and fallbacks reduced overall impact; we have applied a fix and full service has resumed. If you see continued errors, please contact support and include request IDs.

Longer customer explanation (for email or KB):
What happened: A combination of a faulty autoscaling policy interaction and a cache eviction edgecase caused a cascading backlog on a subset of GPU hosts. This increased request queuing and led to request timeouts and occasional 5xx errors. The issue was limited to the eu-west-1 inference cluster and persisted while the controller retried and attempted to re-balance pods.

Who was impacted:
- Primary: tenants pinned to eu-west-1 inference nodes without cross-region fallback enabled.
- Secondary: some globally routed customers experienced transient elevated latency while traffic rebalanced.

Customer impact matrix (quick):
- API availability: ~95–98% for eu-west-1 during window (depending on tenant routing config)
- Streaming sessions: some streams truncated and required client retries
- Embeddings and non-real-time endpoints: largely unaffected

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:18 detection alert (rate of 5xx increased)
- 03:20 incident declared; triage started (SRE + Serving Runtime + CS)
- 03:45 temporary policy change: increased routing to cross-region fallback for eligible tenants
- 04:10 attempted autoscaler reset (partial relief)
- 05:30 confirmed cache eviction race reproducer on staging; created hotfix branch
- 05:55 rolled hotfix to eu-west-1 controller (safe mode)
- 06:05 error rates returned to baseline; monitoring in watch mode

Immediate actions we took: 
- Enabled cross-region fallback for eligible tenants to route traffic to eu-central-1 and us-east-1 where capacity was available.
- Issued a safe-mode scaling policy that blocks aggressive downscales during recovery windows.
- Deployed a targeted controller patch that avoids the cache eviction race and improves queue backpressure signaling.
- Added additional alerting for queue-length spikes ahead of 5xx thresholds.

What customers can do now: 
- If you rely on single-region inference, consider enabling soft cross-region fallback (config flag in the Console) to reduce risk from localized host-level issues.
- For critical low-latency paths, add a short client-side retry with jitter (we recommend up to 2 retries with exponential backoff for 5xx).
- If you saw truncated streaming outputs, request a replay using the support form and include the request IDs and timestamp range; we will prioritize verification.

Key-account outreach script (for AE/CS):
- Opening: "We wanted to reach out proactively about the eu-west-1 disruption on 2026-03-31; our engineering team has resolved the root cause and pushed mitigations. I can walk you through the timeline and any specific requests you saw."
- If asked about data: "There is no indication of data loss or exfiltration; this was a control-plane/queueing issue isolated to inference serving."
- Offer: replay assistance for affected calls, and a short-term SLA credit if a customer had sustained errors above their tolerance (we will evaluate on a case-by-case basis).

Internal operator checklist (to close incident):
- [ ] Confirm monitoring shows baseline (error rate and p50/p95 latency) for 48 hours post-resolution.
- [ ] Run controlled canary with scaled-down traffic and observe queue length under autoscaler stress tests.
- [ ] Merge postmortem PR with root-cause analysis and corrective action items (owner + ETA).
- [ ] Prepare customer-facing closure note (one-paragraph) and update Status Page with resolved/closure message.
- [ ] Identify tenants that had >5% error rate during window and prepare outreach list for CS.

FAQ (anticipated customer questions and short answers):
Q: Was customer data affected?
A: No. This incident affected request routing and queueing; we have no evidence of data loss.

Q: Will you change autoscaling behaviour?
A: Yes — we have adjusted the autoscaler to add more conservative cooldowns and added a guard to prevent certain scale-down sequences that triggered this cascade.

Q: Can we get a credit?
A: We will evaluate SLA credits for customers with verified sustained impact and will coordinate individually through CS.

Open questions / decisions to finalize:
- Decide whether to proactively enable soft cross-region fallback for all new tenants vs. require opt-in. (Product + Privacy review)
- SLA credit policy threshold for this class of transient partial-region outage (Finance + Legal).

Appendix: Suggested one-line closure for status page and email:
Status page closure: "Incident resolved: eu-west-1 inference disruption - full service restored and mitigations deployed as of 2026-03-31 06:05 UTC."
Customer closure email (short): "We’ve completed our investigation into the eu-west-1 disruption on 2026-03-31. Full service has been restored and we’ve deployed fixes to prevent recurrence. If you experienced errors, please reply with request IDs and we’ll prioritize help or replay."

Notes to self (drafting tips):
- Keep customer-facing text succinct and non-technical; provide a technical appendix for large enterprise customers.
- For account outreach, include specific example request IDs where available; customers want evidence we can reproduce.
- Link the postmortem Confluence and the incident Jira in the closure note.

End of doc.
